fact_ea_nasir: Around 1750 BC a customer named Nanni had a complaint about poor-quality copper pressed into clay and sent to the merchant Ea-nāṣir. It's the oldest known written complaint.
fact_needle_shop: The earliest known printed advert is a Song-dynasty printing plate for Liu's Fine Needle Shop in Jinan, China, with a rabbit for a logo.
fact_hopewell: As much as 2,000 years ago, obsidian from Yellowstone reached Hopewell sites in what is now Ohio, about 2,000 miles away.
fact_chaco_cacao: About a thousand years ago, cacao from Mexico reached Pueblo Bonito in what is now New Mexico, at least 1,200 miles away.
fact_pochteca: The Aztec Empire had professional long-distance merchants, the pochteca, who managed its markets and traded beyond its borders.
fact_kultepe: More than 23,000 clay tablets were found in homes at Kültepe in Turkey, where Assyrian merchants kept a trading district nearly 4,000 years ago.
fact_cowry: The shell of the money cowry, a small sea snail, was currency along the trade networks of Africa, South Asia and East Asia.
fact_vending: The earliest known vending machine was described by Hero of Alexandria in the 1st century AD: it took a coin and gave out holy water.
fact_trajan: Trajan's Market in Rome, built around AD 100 to 110, is thought to be the world's oldest shopping mall.
fact_wedgwood: In the 1700s the potter Josiah Wedgwood pioneered money-back guarantees, free delivery, illustrated catalogues and buy one, get one free.
fact_mail_order: The first mail-order catalogues were sent out in 1861 by Pryce Pryce-Jones of Newtown, Wales. They sold woollen goods, delivered by rail.
fact_price_tag: The price tag is credited to John Wanamaker, a Philadelphia shopkeeper, who made it the standard in the 1800s.
fact_trade_mark: The UK's first registered trade mark was the red triangle of the Bass brewery, in 1876.
fact_cash_register: The cash register was invented in 1879 by James Ritty, a saloon owner in Dayton, Ohio, who thought his staff were pocketing the takings.
fact_shopping_cart: The shopping cart dates from 1937. Its inventor, the Oklahoma grocer Sylvan Goldman, started with a basket and wheels on a folding chair.
fact_barcode: The first barcode scanned at a shop checkout was on a pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum, on 26 June 1974 in Troy, Ohio. It rang up 67 cents.
fact_first_web_sale: One of the first things sold online, in 1994, was Sting's album Ten Summoner's Tales.
